title: Entropy-aware session stickiness and decision-graph for staged model rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers running staged model rollouts (canary / A-B) report two pain points: 1) end-users are bouncing between variants when capacity changes or routing policies evolve, causing noisy eval metrics and UX regressions; 2) console controls for rollouts are too coarse (percent traffic split only) and lack knobs to control how long a session should remain pinned to a variant when fallback/degrade paths occur.

Goal: Ship a decision-graph driven routing policy that combines an entropy metric for session assignment with transparent console controls. The feature should: (a) provide deterministic but entropy-aware stickiness so low-variance sessions stay pinned while high-variance cohorts are allowed probabilistic re-assignment, (b) expose TTL and decay strategies in the Console, (c) ensure graceful fallback to compatible model variants based on capability and cost tiers, and (d) surface telemetry to evaluate rollout health and variant churn.

Scope: Product-level design, Console UX, rollout policy schema, recommended defaults for entropy threshold and TTL, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan. Engineering will implement the routing resolver and telemetry hooks (see dependencies). Design will provide Console mockups and copy.

Non-goals: Changing underlying kernel selection, batching algorithms, or model quality evaluation infrastructure (these are out of scope for this ticket and tracked separately).

Definitions: Session entropy = a lightweight metric computed from variant-assignment history and request fingerprint; higher entropy indicates more mixed exposures. Decision-graph = a small state machine evaluated at request time that uses inputs (session entropy, region, tier availability, user pin, canary cohort membership, error rate) to select variant with attenuation to avoid churn.
acceptance_criteria: Product and Design approve Console mockups showing: TTL slider, entropy threshold slider, cohort scope selector (global/org/project), and a readout of expected reassign probability.
Routing policy schema added to API spec: fields for session_ttl_seconds, entropy_threshold, decay_rate, fallback_priority_list, and probabilistic_unpin_enabled.
Default policy shipped: session_ttl_seconds=86400, entropy_threshold=0.35, decay_rate=0.1 per day, probabilistic_unpin_enabled=true with initial reassign_prob=0.05.

Telemetry events defined: session_assigned, session_unpinned, variant_fallback_triggered, entropy_metric_sampled. Dashboards prototype created in Console (per-variant churn, per-cohort entropy histogram, per-route fallback rate).

Canary flow exercise documented: steps to run a canary with 5% traffic and entropy-based stickiness; runbook includes automated rollback if variant fallback rate > 2% over 15 minutes or median latency regresses > 20%.
E2E integration tests added to routing resolver validating deterministic pinning for low-entropy sessions and probabilistic unpin for high-entropy sessions under simulated failover conditions.
notes: Design trade-off: aggressive TTL reduces exposure to regressions but delays metric convergence. We recommend conservative defaults and providing a quick-unpin action in Console.

We should limit entropy computation cost: store a rolling 7-sample assignment history per session and compute a normalized entropy score. Engineering estimate assumes additional ~8 bytes per session in sticky-state store.
Fallback semantics should prefer same-architecture variants (e.g., float32 -> quantized variant of same model) before cross-model fallbacks. Product to propose a compatibility-ranking matrix.
Potential legal/PII note: session identifiers must avoid PII; use hashed request fingerprinting. Security to review hashing policy if customers request deterministic mapping for auditing.
